label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
@Kavya, I’ve thought a lot about whether to respond here. I don’t want to turn a friendship into a public fight, but some details in yesterday’s post are being repeated as fact, including the “40% hike,” so I want to put my side on record.

First, what I got wrong: I knew both candidates were working at SitterNest from day one. I should have called you before we made the offers, not after the second one was accepted. That was careless and unfair to you. I’m sorry. Avoiding that awkward call was easier in the moment, but it wasn’t the right thing to do to a friend.

We went through Foundry91 Cohort 4 together, with your babysitter-booking app SitterNest and my home-tiffin subscription app DabbaDost, through demo day in March 2026. You sat with me until 1 a.m. in the Koramangala office untangling our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I have never forgotten that, and one hiring mistake does not erase how much you’ve helped me.

The facts: We listed a backend developer opening on DabbaDost’s LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to everyone. The first candidate applied on his own on 19 September; the second came through his referral two weeks later. No one from my side DM’d either candidate or approached them privately.

The offers were 22% over their then-current CTC, not 40%. Both joined on 3 November. We also did not promise ESOPs we do not have. DabbaDost has an ESOP pool. It is small, but real, and has been on paper since January.

I messaged you on WhatsApp after the second offer was accepted. I saw it had been read, and then the post came. I understand you were upset; I just wish we could have spoken before it reached LinkedIn.

With 11 startups in one batch, hiring from the same small HSR and Koramangala talent pool, this will keep happening. People apply, refer friends and make their own choices. How we handle those choices still matters.

My suggestion for Foundry91: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before the offer. No veto, no restrictions, no drama—just basic courtesy between founders who know each other. I’ll follow it going forward.

This isn’t me trying to win a comment thread. I want to own my mistake without accepting claims that aren’t true. Kavya, coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you’re okay with it. I respect you, and I’d rather repair the friendship than have the last word.
